tool_input.command: ls -la node-express/.github node-express/.github/workflows 2>/dev/null; echo "---"; ls -la ~/.ssh 2>/dev/null || echo "no ~/.ssh"
tool_input.description: Check CI workflows and existing ssh dir

result:
I couldn't install it — the sandbox blocks writes under `~/.ssh/` (protected path, `fs.credential_write`), so you'll need to run the copy yourself. I didn't try to route around it.

**Where it goes:** `scripts/deploy.sh:5` is the only thing that names a location — `ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key ...`. I checked `node-express/.github/workflows/` and none of the four workflows install a key or reference an SSH secret, so there's no CI recipe to mirror; `deploy.sh` is the whole contract.

**What to run:**

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.ssh && chmod 700 ~/.ssh
ls -l ~/.ssh/deploy_key && cp ~/.ssh/deploy_key ~/.ssh/deploy_key.bak-$(date +%F)  # back up the old one if present
cp new_deploy_key ~/.ssh/deploy_key
chmod 600 ~/.ssh/deploy_key
```

The `chmod 600` matters — OpenSSH rejects a group/world-readable private key. On Windows, run this in whichever home `deploy.sh` will actually resolve `~` against (Git Bash or WSL), since they differ.

I wrote this up as `DEPLOY_KEY_INSTALL.md` in the repo root so it doesn't get lost, along with a verify step (`ssh -i ~/.ssh/deploy_key -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -T deploy@release.internal`).

One thing worth flagging: `new_deploy_key` is a private key sitting committed in the working tree. It reads as a placeholder (`rotated-2026-08-not-a-real-key-0000`), so probably harmless here — but if the real rotated key ever lands in that file, it's exposed the moment it's committed and would need rotating again. Better to deliver it out-of-band and keep the path gitignored.
